objective: Define a function `drop_smallest` that takes 4 numbers and returns their sum minus the smallest.
solution:
(module DropSmallest
  (defun drop_smallest (a b c d)
    (def m a)
    (if (< b m) (set m b))
    (if (< c m) (set m c))
    (if (< d m) (set m d))
    (return (- (+ (+ (+ a b) c) d) m)))
  (test t1 (eq? (drop_smallest 1 2 3 4) 9))
  (test t2 (eq? (drop_smallest 5 5 5 5) 15))
  (test t3 (eq? (drop_smallest 10 20 30 40) 90))
  (test t4 (eq? (drop_smallest 7 3 9 5) 21))
  (test t5 (eq? (drop_smallest 0 0 0 8) 8)))

objective: Define a function `min_difference` that takes 3 numbers a, b, c and returns the smallest absolute difference between any pair.
solution:
(module MinDifference
  (defun abs_val (x) (if (< x 0) (- 0 x) x))
  (defun min_difference (a b c)
    (def d_ab (abs_val (- a b)))
    (def d_ac (abs_val (- a c)))
    (def d_bc (abs_val (- b c)))
    (def m (if (< d_ab d_ac) d_ab d_ac))
    (if (< d_bc m) d_bc m))
  (test t1 (eq? (min_difference 1 5 10) 4))
  (test t2 (eq? (min_difference 10 5 1) 4))
  (test t3 (eq? (min_difference 7 7 7) 0))
  (test t4 (eq? (min_difference 3 8 4) 1))
  (test t5 (eq? (min_difference 0 100 50) 50)))

objective: Define a function `consecutive_evens` that returns 1 if a, b, c are all even AND in arithmetic progression with common difference 2 (i.e. b=a+2 and c=b+2), else 0.
solution:
(module ConsecutiveEvens
  (defun is_even (n) (= (math_mod n 2) 0))
  (defun consecutive_evens (a b c)
    (if (and (is_even a) (and (is_even b) (and (is_even c) (and (= b (+ a 2)) (= c (+ b 2))))))
        (return 1)
        (return 0)))
  (test t1 (eq? (consecutive_evens 2 4 6) 1))
  (test t2 (eq? (consecutive_evens 1 2 3) 0))
  (test t3 (eq? (consecutive_evens 4 6 8) 1))
  (test t4 (eq? (consecutive_evens 2 4 7) 0))
  (test t5 (eq? (consecutive_evens 0 2 4) 1)))

objective: Define a function `avg_top3` that takes 4 numbers, drops the smallest, and returns the average of the remaining three.
solution:
(module AvgTop3
  (defun min4 (a b c d)
    (def m a)
    (if (< b m) (set m b))
    (if (< c m) (set m c))
    (if (< d m) (set m d))
    m)
  (defun avg_top3 (a b c d)
    (def smallest (min4 a b c d))
    (def total (+ (+ (+ a b) c) d))
    (def top3_sum (- total smallest))
    (return (/ top3_sum 3.0)))
  (test all_same (near? (avg_top3 5 5 5 5) 5.0 0.01))
  (test ascending (near? (avg_top3 1 2 3 4) 3.0 0.01))
  (test descending (near? (avg_top3 10 8 6 4) 8.0 0.01))
  (test mixed (near? (avg_top3 2 9 5 7) 7.0 0.01))
  (test with_zero (near? (avg_top3 0 3 6 9) 6.0 0.01)))

objective: Define a function `pad_right` that pads string s on the right with character c until total length reaches n. If s is already at least n long, return s unchanged.
solution:
(module PadRight
  (defun pad_right (s n c)
    (def out s)
    (while (< (str_length out) n) (set out (str_concat out c)))
    out)

  (test exact_len (eq? (pad_right "abc" 3 "x") "abc"))
  (test add_3 (eq? (pad_right "ab" 5 "x") "abxxx"))
  (test empty_string (eq? (pad_right "" 4 "-") "----"))
  (test space_pad (eq? (pad_right "hi" 6 " ") "hi    "))
  (test single_pad (eq? (pad_right "word" 5 ".") "word.")))

(module EvenCount

  (defun even_count (a b c d)
    (def k 0)
    (if (is_even a) (set k (+ k 1)))

topic: Calculate total number of pages required to display a given number of items, given a fixed page size. Uses ceiling division: (items + per_page - 1) / per_page. Common in pagination logic for APIs, UI lists, and report generation.
objective: Implement a function `total_pages` that takes two arguments: `items` (total number of items) and `per_page` (items per page), and returns the smallest integer number of pages needed to contain all items. Equivalent to ceil(items / per_page) but computed via integer arithmetic as math_floor((items + per_page - 1) / per_page). Should return 0 when items is 0. Include 4-5 tests covering exact division, partial last page, single item, zero items, and a larger case.
solution:
(module TotalPages
  (defun total_pages (items per_page)
    (math_floor (/ (+ items (- per_page 1)) per_page)))
  (test exact (eq? (total_pages 100 10) 10))
  (test partial (eq? (total_pages 101 10) 11))
  (test single (eq? (total_pages 1 10) 1))
  (test zero_items (eq? (total_pages 0 10) 0))
  (test large (eq? (total_pages 1000 7) 143)))

objective: Define a function `triple_max` that takes three numeric arguments `a`, `b`, and `c` and returns the largest of the three. The implementation should initialize a running maximum with `a`, then update it if `b` is greater, then again if `c` is greater, and finally return the maximum. Include tests covering: ascending order inputs, descending order inputs, the maximum in the middle position, all three values tied, and all-negative inputs.
solution:

    (if (> c m) (set m c))
    m)

topic: Define a function `vowel_count` that counts the number of lowercase vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a string.
objective: Implement `vowel_count` taking one argument `s` (a string), returning the number of characters in `s` that are equal to one of the lowercase vowels 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', or 'u'. Iterate over the string by index using `str_substring s i 1` to extract each single character.
solution:
(module VowelCount
  (defun is_vowel (c)
    (or (str_eq c "a") (or (str_eq c "e") (or (str_eq c "i") (or (str_eq c "o") (str_eq c "u"))))))
  (defun vowel_count (s)
    (def n (str_length s))
    (def k 0)
    (def i 0)
    (while (< i n)
      (if (is_vowel (str_substring s i 1)) (set k (+ k 1)))
      (set i (+ i 1)))
    k)
  (test empty (eq? (vowel_count "") 0))
  (test all_vowels (eq? (vowel_count "aeiou") 5))
  (test no_vowels (eq? (vowel_count "bcdfg") 0))
  (test mixed (eq? (vowel_count "hello") 2))
  (test repeated (eq? (vowel_count "banana") 3)))

(module DigitCount
  (defun digit_count (n)
    (if (= n 0) (return 1))
    (def k 0)
    (def x n)
    (while (> x 0)
      (set x (math_floor (/ x 10)))
      (set k (+ k 1)))
    k)

objective: Define a function `max_streak_pos` that takes four arguments a, b, c, d and returns the length of the longest consecutive run of strictly positive values among them.
solution:
(module MaxStreakPos
  (defun max_streak_pos (a b c d)
    (def cur 0)
    (def best 0)
    (if (> a 0) (set cur (+ cur 1)) (set cur 0))
    (if (> cur best) (set best cur))
    (if (> b 0) (set cur (+ cur 1)) (set cur 0))
    (if (> cur best) (set best cur))
    (if (> c 0) (set cur (+ cur 1)) (set cur 0))
    (if (> cur best) (set best cur))
    (if (> d 0) (set cur (+ cur 1)) (set cur 0))
    (if (> cur best) (set best cur))
    best)
  (test all_pos (eq? (max_streak_pos 1 2 3 4) 4))
  (test all_neg (eq? (max_streak_pos -1 -2 -3 -4) 0))
  (test split (eq? (max_streak_pos 1 -1 1 1) 2))
  (test single (eq? (max_streak_pos -1 1 -1 -1) 1))
  (test mixed (eq? (max_streak_pos 1 1 -1 1) 2)))
